Tosafot on Bava Batra 95b:6:1.hebrew: חד אמר מקבל - תימה: לדידיה, אמאי מוקי רב זביד מתניתין כר' אושעיא, ובדאמר ליה "מרתף זה של יין אני מוכר לך", וא"ל "למקפה"? לוקי מתני' בלא א"ל "למקפה", ובדאמר ליה "מרתף של יין" סתם:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 95b:6:1.english: One said: He must accept [the wine] - It is puzzling: according to him, why does Rav Zevid establish the Mishnah as following R. Oshaya, and [as dealing with a case] where [the seller] said to him, "I am selling you this cellar of wine," and [the buyer] said to him, "[It is] for a mikpah"? Let him establish the Mishnah [as dealing with a case] where [the buyer] did not say to him "for a mikpah," and where [the seller] said to him simply "a cellar of wine," without specification:

Tosafot on Bava Batra 95b:6:2.hebrew: וחד אמר לא מקבל - קשה לרשב"א: א"כ אמאי נקט ר' חייא לעיל "המוכר חבית של יין לחבירו נותן לו יין שכולו יפה"? מאי איריא חבית? אפי' מרתף נמי! ויש מפרשים: לרבותא נקטיה, כדפירש הקונטרס לעיל:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 95b:6:2.english: "And one said he does not accept" - Rashba found this difficult: If so, why did R. Chiyya state above, "One who sells a barrel of wine to his fellow must give him wine that is entirely good"? Why specifically a barrel? Even a cellar [should be the same]! And some explain: He stated it to teach a novelty, as the Kuntres (Rashbam) explained above:
